quiz.why: Momentum change per second.

quiz.q: Propulsive efficiency is highest when v_e/v₀ is…
Most air in a high-bypass turbofan…
quiz.why: The fan stream.

quiz.q: I_sp is measured in…
quiz.why: Thrust per weight flow of propellant.

quiz.q: Jets push against the air behind them.
quiz.why: They accelerate air through the engine; the reaction to that is thrust.

quiz.q: Faster exhaust always means a better engine.
quiz.why: For efficiency, exhaust speed should be close to flight speed.

quiz.q: Specific impulse is a speed.
quiz.why: It is measured in seconds; I_sp × g₀ is an effective exhaust speed.

quiz.q: A turbofan moves 500 kg/s of air from 250 m/s to 320 m/s. Find thrust and propulsive efficiency. Give your answer in kN.
An engine makes 100 kN while burning 2.5 kg/s of fuel. Find its I_sp.
quiz.why: ≈ 4,079 s. Air-breathers beat rockets on this measure because they do not carry their oxidizer.

quiz.q: Find the thrust for ṁ = 200 kg/s, v₀ = 200 m/s, v_e = 300 m/s. Give your answer in kN.
quiz.why: 20 kN.

quiz.q: 1.0, but the thrust is zero: efficiency and thrust trade off.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Find η_p when v_e = v₀.

quiz.q: They move a large mass of air slowly, which raises propulsive efficiency and cuts fuel burn and noise.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Why do airliners use high-bypass turbofans?

quiz.q: v_e = 600 m/s, η_p ≈ 0.59: much less efficient.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. A turbojet makes the same 35 kN with 100 kg/s of air at v₀ = 250 m/s. What exhaust speed does it need, and what is η_p?

quiz.q: Higher propulsive efficiency is a direct fuel and CO₂ saving. Every kilogram of jet fuel burned produces about 3.16 kg of CO₂ (the fuel’s carbon combined with oxygen from the air; see Unit 10), so efficiency gains add up over an engine’s decades of service.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Sustainable aviation fuel, made from wastes and biomass, is blended to match conventional jet fuel’s properties for safe operation. NASA notes that SAF does not release new CO₂ into the environment.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Every engine makes thrust by accelerating a mass flow: F = ṁ(v_e − v₀) for an air-breathing engine (ignoring fuel mass and pressure terms).
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Propulsive efficiency η_p = 2/(1 + v_e/v₀): moving a lot of air a little is more efficient than moving a little air a lot. That is why turbofans have huge fans.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Turbojet: all air passes through the core. Turbofan: most air bypasses the core through the fan. Turboprop: a propeller driven by a gas turbine.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Specific impulse I_sp = F/(ṁ_fuel g₀) measures thrust per fuel weight flow, in seconds.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: This unit asks you to: Use the momentum thrust equation.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.
